title: Priority lanes and quota fences — UX notes & backlog
content:
TL;DR
We need a compact UX pattern for: (a) surfacing per-key and per-route quota fences; (b) letting operators create "priority lanes" that bypass soft throttles for tiered customers; and (c) an emergency "quarantine" flow (token quarantine + temporary rollback) when an API key goes hot. This doc records initial wireframe sketches, open questions, acceptance criteria, and a prioritized backlog for a first pass MVP.

Context and motivation
- Problem: customers frequently ask for more granular control than global rate limits — they want to allocate budget or priority by credential, route, or SLA class, and to see attribution/impact in analytics at the same time.
- Observed behaviors from CS: two common asks: 1) reserve headroom for critical keys (payment/checkout flows) during bursts, 2) quickly isolate a compromised key without impacting other traffic.
- Goal: give ops product-teams first-class controls + clear observability so they can both configure and validate changes quickly.

High-level product goals
- G1: Configure per-key/per-route "quota fences" (hard limits) and soft throttles (graceful shedding) with a simple surface.
- G2: Create "priority lanes" that can be attached to keys or routes. Priority lanes get served preferentially during contention.
- G3: Emergency quarantine: single-click isolate/rollback keys and automatically surface impact and recommended next steps.
- G4: Analytics tie-in: show before/after token-level economics (cost delta, latency, error rates) for any change.

Wireframe ideas (sketch notes)
1) Quota Fences panel (left column)
   - Compact list of active fences: name, scope (key/route/all), limit (tokens/min or calls/min), enforcement type (hard | soft), current usage bar, remaining headroom numeric.
   - Action buttons: edit, duplicate, temporarily disable, history (last 7 days).
   - Inline indicator for scope collisions (e.g., a key-level fence that is tighter than its route-level parent).
2) Priority Lanes (center column — main canvas)
   - Visual lanes like network queues: lane name, priority weight (0-100), attached keys/routes (chips), fallback policy (downgrade to smaller model|queue), escalation rules.
   - Drag-and-drop UI to move keys between lanes in the wireframe (prototype for internal demo).
   - Slot for a small simulation control: "run 5m burst simulation" showing expected token throughput and estimated tail latency.
3) Emergency Quarantine (right column — contextual)
   - Quick actions for a selected API key: Quarantine (soft), Quarantine (hard), Re-enable. 
   - When quarantined: open a modal that shows top 5 affected routes and predicted SLA impact, plus a suggested automatic fallback (route->backup model).
   - Provide a one-click rollback that re-applies the previous quota/fence config (audit trail required).

Analytics integrations (notes)
- Per-change preview: estimate TPS and cost delta for the next 1h and 24h based on rolling metrics.
- Attribution table: top 10 routes contributing to a key's token consumption, with trend sparkline.
- Alerting hooks: new per-fence alert type (near-headroom, sustained-below-threshold, sudden-spike). Link to per-route alerting UI (see RI-3308).
- Sample queries needed from infra: tokens_by_key_route(start, end, aggregation=1m) and residual_headroom_by_key.

Interactions and microcopy
- Emphasize safe defaults: when creating a hard fence, suggest a "dry-run" option (evaluate for 24h before enforcement).
- Modal copy for quarantine: "Quarantine will stop outgoing inference for this key for N minutes. Other keys unaffected. Use 'hard' to immediately block, 'soft' to route to fallback models."
- Inline help links to docs: "What is a priority lane?" and "How do fences interact?"

Open questions (needs engineering/product decisions)
- Q1: Enforcement order when multiple fences apply: route-level vs key-level vs global. Preference: most-specific wins (key > route > global). Need infra confirmation for atomic enforcement.
- Q2: Billing implications for priority lanes (are priority-lane served tokens billed differently?). Need finance input. Ticket: RI-3221.
- Q3: Simulation accuracy: how accurate can a 5m simulated burst be without reserving capacity? Work with serving-runtime on a light-weight estimator.
- Q4: RBAC: who can quarantine keys? Default: org-admin + security role. Need to map to existing IAM model.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- AC1: UI to create/edit/delete quota fences with at least key and route scope + enforcement type.
- AC2: UI to create basic priority lane and attach keys or routes.
- AC3: Quarantine flow that blocks traffic for a key (soft/hard) and records an audit event.
- AC4: Analytics panel shows per-key, per-route token usage and top contributors; supports 1h/24h pivot.
- AC5: All changes are auditable and linked to a change history view.

Backlog (prioritized)
- P0: Quota fences CRUD + enforcement (RI-3308).
- P0: Quarantine hard/soft implementation + audit trail.
- P1: Priority lane weights + simple scheduler integration.
- P1: Burst simulation engine (estimator only).
- P2: Per-change cost preview (finance integration).
- P2: Drag-and-drop lane editor (nice-to-have for demo).
- P3: Route-level automatic fallback rules (auto-swizzle model variant).

Data & infra constraints
- Need a short retention window for per-minute token counts (1m granularity, 30 days) to drive the analytics pivots and simulations.
- Need a lightweight enforcement API: attach fence to key/route ID -> runtime returns enforcement token.
- Prefer eventually-consistent UI for open fences; critical for quarantine to be strongly consistent.

Implementation notes (engineering handoff)
- API suggestions: POST /admin/fences {scope: 'key'|'route', id: <id>, limit: 1000, unit: 'tokens/min', enforcement: 'hard'|'soft', dry_run: bool}
- Quarantine endpoints: POST /admin/keys/:id/quarantine {mode: 'soft'|'hard', duration_minutes: int, reason: string} -> returns change_id for audit.
- Analytics endpoints needed: GET /metrics/tokens?group_by=key,route&range=24h&interval=1m
- Audit events to capture: who, when, action, previous_config, predicted_impact_snapshot.

Edge cases and safety nets
- When multiple priority lanes conflict, show warnings and require confirmation if total guaranteed capacity exceeds reservations.
- If a user quarantines a key in error, provide a 2-step undo (re-enable + brief modal explaining consequences).
- Avoid accidental global outages: require additional confirmation for operations that affect more than N keys or more than X% of traffic.

Runbook sketch for customer success and SRE
- If a quarantine causes elevated errors: auto-run diagnostics: (1) list other keys on same org, (2) top 5 failing routes, (3) suggest soft-enable fallback per-route.
- Runbook steps for rollback: identify change_id -> click rollback -> confirm -> monitor 5m.

Next steps (this week)
- Prototype low-fidelity wireframes in Figma (Maya) and spike basic backend API prototype (Chris).
- Sync with infra: confirm enforcement semantics (Liam from serving-runtime).
- Draft a short customer-facing one-pager for CS so they can demo priority lanes to 2 pilot customers.

Unresolved UX bits for review
- Visual encoding for 'soft' vs 'hard' (color + icon?). Tentative: hard = red lock icon, soft = amber feather icon.
- How to show cumulative effect across nested fences without cluttering the page — suggestion: hover-to-expand combined rules.

Notes to self / meeting follow-ups
- Embed a small prototype that shows moving an API key from "standard" lane to "priority" and show projected 95th percentile latency change.
- Bring finance into the meeting on Thursday for pricing implications and billing labels.
- Pull sample datasets for keys from customer sandbox to demo in the March product review.

Rough timeline
- Week 1: wireframes + API shape + backlog tickets.
- Week 2–3: backend enforcement prototype + analytics MVP.
- Week 4: internal demo + CS pilot.

Quick links referenced in doc:
- Ticket RI-3221 (billing for priority lanes)
- Ticket RI-3308 (per-fence alerting integration)
- Confluence RFC: Quota Puzzles (link above).

End.
